claims.text: The specific allegations in that statement: a fabricated photograph purporting to show Warren with John Lennon; a USAF Form 490 medical appointment card whose notation 'OPTI/RET BURN/EXP' is attributed to a 'Dr. Echols' whom Robbins says was an orthopaedic surgeon rather than an ophthalmologist, making the notation impossible; signature inconsistencies on an in-processing sheet; and testimonial letters attributed to airmen Steve LaPlume and Steve Longero that Robbins says were never sent.

claims.text: What he examined and what he concedes: military paperwork supplied by Warren, 'mostly Xerox copies with some originals', and the handwritten letter Warren wrote to his mother in January 1981, which Robbins accepts as authentic while arguing it 'does not mean that everything else Warren has said or written follows in kind'.

label: Peter Robbins
narrative: Peter Robbins is a node because the strongest evidence against one of this cluster's witnesses is a document he wrote, and a claim of that weight should not hang off an unattributed note. He spent twenty-nine years as Larry Warren's co-author and public defender, and then on 13 June 2017 published a statement setting out, item by item, why he no longer believed what he had defended: an allegedly fabricated photograph, an allegedly altered USAF medical form, signatures that do not match, letters that were never sent. What makes the statement usable rather than merely dramatic is that it concedes: he accepts the authenticity of Warren's January 1981 letter home and says so, and he notes that the paperwork he examined came to him from Warren and was mostly photocopies. Four months after he published, the book's publisher suspended its distribution. Robbins also records that he has no further interest in researching the case, which is a limitation on him as a source and is carried here as one.

timeline.text: Robbins publishes a statement alleging that Larry Warren fabricated a photograph with John Lennon, altered a USAF Form 490 whose ophthalmic notation is attributed to a physician Robbins found to be an orthopaedic surgeon, produced an in-processing sheet with mismatched signatures, and attributed testimonial letters to two named airmen that were never sent. He accepts as authentic Warren's January 1981 letter to his mother.
